identityReview: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, born March 29, 1944 Accra, Ghanaian lawyer and NPP politician; distinct from father Edward, former ceremonial president/chief justice. University of Ghana economics bachelor 1967, English bar 1971/Ghana bar 1975; bar credentials not separate verified law degree. Cabinet 2001–2003 justice/attorney-general, 2003–2007 foreign affairs; three MP elections without adopting inconsistent tenure dates. Ghana president first inaugurated January 7, 2017, second January 7, 2021, handed over to returning Mahama January 7, 2025. ECOWAS Authority chair September 7, 2020–July 3, 2022 differs from Commission leadership. No current government office inferred from meeting successor.
lifeStatusEvidence: MyJoyOnline November 17, 2026 account confirms completed meeting at his Nima, Accra home with incumbent president Mahama, attended by Mahama staff. No agreement or appointment published; does not imply return to office.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read historical GNA and GABI biographies, explicitly Wikipedia-derived university alumni entry, Ghana UN Mission inauguration, Reuters handover, relevant Finance Ministry budget sections, Harvard policy-case introduction/implementation sections, IMF rendered approval content, ECOWAS election release, GBC actual election report, MFWA succession statement and MyJoyOnline latest completed meeting. Read Commons/Flickr metadata and linked original licence, no photo pixels.
corrections: Read GNA historical October 2020 profile: March 29, 1944 Accra birth; father Edward held ceremonial presidency 1970–1972; University of Ghana economics 1964–1967, bachelor degree; English bar 1971, Ghanaian bar 1975, Coudert Brothers and Accra practice, 1979 firm, NPP 1992, three parliamentary elections, justice/attorney-general 2001, foreign minister 2003, government exit 2007, 2008/2012 presidential defeats and 2016 victory/2017 inauguration. Its 1996–2007 MP range conflicts with other accounts and conflates election/service; no exact parliamentary tenure adopted. Praise of personal peace-making, court automation or human-rights success is not independently audited. Criminal-libel repeal role reported here, no exhaustive legislative/docket audit claimed.

Read University of Ghana alumni page, which explicitly credits Wikipedia. Supports 1967 BSc(Econ) wording but is not independent primary academic evidence. Historical current-president wording is stale. Oxford unfinished attendance and Inner/Middle Temple distinctions not used to invent an Oxford qualification or formal law degree. Birth/education cross-checked with GNA; no original diploma authenticated.

Read UN Global Compact GABI participant biography: three MP terms, attorney-general/justice minister 2001–2003, foreign minister April 2003–July 2007, 2008 runoff defeat, 2012 defeat and subsequent acceptance of court result, 2016 victory, December 7, 2020 re-election and January 7, 2021 inauguration. Current-president heading is historical despite 2026 website footer. Use year-level cabinet dates, avoid unsupported exact appointment day. MP wording 1997–2008 not silently merged with GNA conflicting range. No detailed five-to-four judgment interpretation or electoral vote-total arithmetic asserted.

Read Ghana UN Mission report of January 7, 2021 second and final inauguration, Bawumia continuing vice-president, December 7, 2020 election and January 7, 2017 first inauguration. Page uses both January 6 and January 7, 2025 endpoint language; dossier describes independently documented January 7 handover without asserting exact constitutional midnight. Published vote totals not used because unnecessary and not separately reconciled.

Read Reuters January 7, 2025 handover account: Mahama actually sworn in after December 2024 election, Akufo-Addo leaves after two terms. Separates current successor from predecessor and past 2017 transfer. Economic challenges provide context, not automatic personal criminal responsibility. Current sidebar/sidebar dates not treated as article updates; only relevant handover facts used.

Read relevant education and industry sections of Finance Ministry 2018 Citizens’ Budget: Free SHS began September 2017 for first-year students, later-cohort expansion planned; One District One Factory launched August 25, 2017, proposal viability review and selection. Proposed factories/jobs, planned 2018 spending and claimed 2017 outputs are distinct. Do not assert every district achieved operational factory or treat forecast employment as realised. Later PDF hosting/crawl date not budget year; no exhaustive line-by-line budget or independent financial audit claimed.

Read 2025 Harvard Ministerial Leadership case-study introduction and implementation sections: policy mandated by Akufo-Addo, delivered through Education Minister Prempeh and team, September 2017 rollout, eligible secondary pupils, fee/support scope and infrastructure/quality constraints. Case study based on interviews with programme participants, not independent experimental proof of all reported impacts. It explicitly does not represent institutional endorsement of conclusions. No universal elimination of inequality or independently verified enrolment effect size asserted.

Read IMF-hosted May 17, 2023 approval content as rendered structured text: initial 36-month ECF, SDR 2.242 billion/about US$3 billion, immediate availability SDR 451.4 million/about US$600 million; macro stability/debt sustainability and restructuring. External shocks exacerbated pre-existing fiscal/debt weaknesses; no single-cause claim. Approval is not full disbursement or completed crisis recovery. Later extension/reviews are separate, so initial duration not asserted as unchanged current programme duration.

Read ECOWAS official announcement: elected by 57th Authority summit, replacing Niger’s Mahamadou Issoufou. Body dateline September 9 and page September 10 are release dates, not substituted for actual election date September 7 confirmed contemporaneously by GBC. Authority chair is not Commission president.

Read GBC September 7, 2020 report and embedded Ministry of Information announcement text confirming election that Monday at Niamey summit. Did not play linked acceptance audio or claim independent inspection of original social-media account. Distinguishes election date from ECOWAS later release and predecessor Issoufou from successor Embaló.

Read MFWA July 7, 2022 statement: Embaló elected July 3 at 61st summit, succeeds Akufo-Addo after two terms, regional coups/security challenges remain. Unrelated sentence incorrectly sequences Embaló February 2020 inauguration after a December 2021 election; do not adopt that chronology. Positive endorsement is advocacy, not independent outcome evaluation. July 3 succession is corroborated by GNA search preview and contemporaneous draft communiqué context, not a claim those full final primary proceedings were inspected.

Read MyJoyOnline November 17, 2026 completed-meeting report: incumbent Mahama visits former president at Nima residence with Julius Debrah and Stan Xoese Dogbe; national/international matters discussed. No specific agreement, new post, return to presidency or motive inferred. Actual article text supports life/activity status; image markers are not visual identity review.
